style: factual clickbait for China finance audience

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一

briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：教皇总在我度假时出事，这次我梦到了
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
我梦到教皇去世，结果真出事了

subtitles.zh: 教皇有个很妙的传统，就是毁掉我的假期。
subtitles.en: The Pope sort of had a great tradition of ruining my vacations.

subtitles.zh: 他要么说些非常重要的话，要么不幸地健康出状况。
subtitles.en: Like he would either say something very important or unfortunately his health would dip.

subtitles.zh: 我度假时总会出事，所以我总是从美国、从任何地方赶回来。
subtitles.en: Something would always happen when I was on vacation, so I was constantly coming back from America, from wherever I was.

subtitles.zh: 这次我在托斯卡纳海岸的梅德马，非常美。
subtitles.en: So in this time I was up in Medema, which is on the Tuscan coast. It was very beautiful.

subtitles.zh: 说起来很疯狂，但这是真的，我梦到教皇去世了，然后我半夜醒来。
subtitles.en: And I actually, this sounds very crazy, but it's true, I dreamt that the Pope had died, right? And I woke up in the middle of the night.

subtitles.zh: 我说，天哪，我刚梦到教皇去世了。我妻子转头说，不，只是你总想着教皇，对吧？
subtitles.en: And I said, oh my god, I just dreamt that the Pope had died. And my wife turned to me and she said, no, it's just that you're always thinking about the Pope, right?

subtitles.zh: 再说，为我辩护一下，教皇确实去世了，对吧？所以我们俩心有灵犀。
subtitles.en: And then again, in my defense, the Pope had died, right? So we were on some wavelength, the two of us.

subtitles.zh: 总之，我赶回罗马，用我女儿的笔记本电脑，我坐前座，她和狗坐后座，我儿子和其他人也在车里。
subtitles.en: Anyway, so rushed back to Rome, and on my daughter's laptop, and I was in the front seat, she was in the back with the dog, my son, some other people were in that car.

subtitles.zh: 有点像小丑车，我在前面极度紧张。
subtitles.en: It was a bit of a clown car, me extremely stressed out in the front.

subtitles.zh: 但随后开始了非常非常忙碌、重要的几周。
subtitles.en: But then began a very, very, very hectic, important couple of weeks.

current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
权威可协商，反叛也来自梵蒂冈

subtitles.zh: 谈谈梵蒂冈在当今罗马生活中的重要性。
subtitles.en: Talk about the importance of Vatican plays in life in Rome today.

subtitles.zh: 而你，一个来自皇后区新鲜草原的人，之前真的得恶补很多这些东西。
subtitles.en: And the great which you, a guy from Fresh Meadows, Queens, really had to bone up on a lot of the stuff, you know, before.

subtitles.zh: 是的，天主教会渗透在意大利的一切中，对吧？它曾统治这里。
subtitles.en: Yeah, yeah, I mean, so the Catholic Church sort of imbues everything in Italy, right? I mean, it ran the place.

subtitles.zh: 教皇国，中部地区曾归教皇管辖。他就是国王，你仍能在很多方面看到这一点。
subtitles.en: The papal states, the middle of the country was under the Pope. He was the king, and you still see it in many, many different ways.

subtitles.zh: 我遇到的一个方面是权威。所以一切都可以协商，对吧？
subtitles.en: One way that I sort of ran into it is authority. So everything is sort of negotiable, right?

subtitles.zh: 我爱我的人民，所以这有好有坏，对吧？
subtitles.en: I love my people, so there's positives and negatives to this, right?

subtitles.zh: 但比如，就连交通警察也是。如果你停车停得很糟，我妻子是出了名的停车差。
subtitles.en: But like, you know, even your traffic cop, right? If you park parking very badly, and my wife is an infamously bad parker.

subtitles.zh: 我会对她说，停得真好但地方不对，我会说，这不是停车位。
subtitles.en: And I would say to her, a wonderful parker but in a bad place, and I would say to her, you know, this is not a spot.

subtitles.zh: 有个交警走过来，她说他理解。事实上就像谈判，说没别的地方可去，他就说好吧。
subtitles.en: And there's like a vigile, there's a traffic cop coming over, and she say he understands. And in fact there was like a negotiation, like there's nowhere else to go, and he'd say okay.

subtitles.zh: 这在某种程度上非常天主教，对吧？非常人性。就像一切，负面的话最终会变成贿赂。
subtitles.en: And that's very, very Catholic in a way, right? It's very human. It's like everything, you know, in a negative way you end up with bribery.

subtitles.zh: 通常你知道，但正面的话，如果有情有可原的情况，它们很重要，对吧？
subtitles.en: And you know, usually you know, but in the positive way you can sort of, you know, if there are extenuating circumstances, they matter, right?

subtitles.zh: 这是我一直接触到它的一种方式。
subtitles.en: And so that's one way that I constantly came into contact with it.

subtitles.zh: 但另一方面，意大利人也极其反权威。
subtitles.en: But on the flip side, Italians are also extremely anti-authoritarian.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这也来自梵蒂冈。他们长期不喜欢梵蒂冈指手画脚。
subtitles.en: And I think that also comes from the Vatican. I think that they didn't like having the Vatican telling them what to do for a long time.

subtitles.zh: 所以意大利作为一个国家是回应梵蒂冈而诞生的。它不想要梵蒂冈。
subtitles.en: And so Italy as a country is born in response to the Vatican. It doesn't want the Vatican.

subtitles.zh: 是的，所以一切。跟他谈谈报道教皇选举会议是什么感觉。
subtitles.en: Yeah, so everything. Talk to him about what it's like to cover a conclave.

Operating rule: 二极管法则
- A candidate is usable only if one emotion pole is unmistakable and emotion_tension is at least 8/10.
- The six permitted poles are: unexpected reversal, pleasant surprise, strong doubt, finally-someone-said-it candor, verified words-versus-actions contrast, and fact-based pride in a Chinese comparative advantage.
- Do not split the emotion across several mild ideas. Pick one pole and push it to the factual limit.
- A question mark is not emotion. "前景如何", "回报路径在哪", "能否实现", "面临哪些挑战", "回报存疑", and "释放什么信号" score at most 4 unless they contain a concrete contradiction or consequence.

Angle rules:
- surprise_reversal: state the familiar baseline, then expose the source claim that reverses it. Do not turn a baseline contrast into "改口" unless research.position_change.supported is true with at least two independent sources.
- outsider_candor: use only when a foreign institution/expert says something unusually direct. Keep the identity contrast in evidence_basis and viewer_reaction, then realize it in final copy by placing the specific surprising claim against its consequence. - words_vs_actions: use only when research.words_vs_actions.supported is true and independent_source_count is at least 2. Show the two exact sides in question form. Never directly call anyone a liar.
- china_advantage: use only when research.china_advantage.supported is true. Put the concrete Chinese advantage or the foreign competitor's forced response in the foreground. The emotional direction must favor China.
- authority_breaks_consensus: the authority must be recognizable to a China audience, or be labeled by a meaningful role. Do not lead with an obscure romanized name.
- concrete_stakes: expose a specific number, forced choice, consequence, or who gains/loses. Generic importance is not a stake.

Writing rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Produce exactly four candidates per clip and use at least three different angle_id values when the evidence permits.
- Each candidate has exactly three short title lines. Think cover blocks, not a newspaper sentence.
- Ideal line lengths are 3-10, 4-12, and 5-14 Chinese characters. Full title is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- The title must reveal enough familiar context to create a small information gap, then withhold the explanation supplied by the video.
- Prefer concrete verbs and consequences: 逼急、藏不住、说透、砍半. Use only when facts support them. "改口" requires research.position_change.supported with two independent sources; words-versus-actions phrases require research.words_vs_actions.supported with two independent sources.
- Do not mechanically copy examples or proper nouns from instructions. Derive every noun, number, actor, and comparison from this clip and its evidence card.
- angle_id, emotion_pole, and viewer_reaction are private editorial metadata. Never copy their wording into title or title_lines.
- Final cover structure should be [specific subject] / [unexpected fact or comparison] / [concrete unresolved consequence], not [speaker category] / [editorial label] / [topic].
- If a person or institution is genuinely recognizable, use its verified proper name. If it is not recognizable, omit the identity and lead with the subject and fact; do not replace it with generic labels such as 外资策略师 or 海外专家.
- For names and technical terms, use only the current clip's verified title_label. Never use official_zh/legal company names as cover copy, and never invent a Chinese transliteration when title_label is empty or English.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is a source label, not the expert or actor. Company legal suffixes do not belong in a title.
- For China-related clips, never attack China or imply national decline. Favor confidence, competence, policy room, industrial strength, cost advantage, talent, resilience, and competitors being forced to respond.
- If the clip is negative about China and no constructive factual angle exists, use a neutral mechanism question instead of nationalist or doom framing.
- Forbidden title words: 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.
- Never use 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了.
- Do not mention sensitive geopolitical or military topics.

KC comment rules:
- comment starts with KC评论： and adds context, consequence, or the next fact to watch in 16-34 Chinese characters. Do not repeat the title.
- subtitle_comments contains one item for every input subtitle index, grounded in that exact subtitle rather than a generic clip slogan.
- Each subtitle comment starts with KC评论： and is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters after the prefix, with a complete ending.
- Adjacent subtitle comments must vary between evidence, implication, tension, consequence, and context.
- All highlight strings must be exact substrings of their corresponding title/comment.

briefs.speaker: Jason Horowitz
briefs.speaker_context: Rome bureau chief for The New York Times, author of 'The Italian Job'
briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：意大利是政治实验室，从贝卢斯科尼到梅洛尼
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
从贝卢斯科尼到梅洛尼，变化中藏着未来

subtitles.zh: 这有点矛盾，因为意大利其实变化不大。
subtitles.en: It's sort of a paradox because Italy doesn't really change much.

subtitles.zh: 它的结构，对意大利人来说重要的是继承法不变，房地产不动，对吧？
subtitles.en: And it's sort of structure, you know, the important things for Italians are that your inheritance laws are the same, your real estate isn't touched, right?

subtitles.zh: 他们非常保守。但这意味着他们会让任何人尝试任何事，对吧？
subtitles.en: They're very conservative. But that means that they will let anybody try anything, right?

subtitles.zh: 所以他们总在寻找新东西。看这25年，从贝卢斯科尼开始，他是第一个媒体大亨政治家。
subtitles.en: And so they're always looking for something new. And so if you look over the 25 years, you go from Berlusconi, who was, you know, the first mogul, media mogul politician.

subtitles.zh: 然后到左翼，极左。再到互联网上诞生的民粹主义者，对吧？
subtitles.en: And then you go to left, you know, far, far left. You go to populists who were born on the internet, right?

subtitles.zh: 所有这些新事物。现在乔治亚·梅洛尼，代表了二战后出生、曾被排除在外的后法西斯主义者的回归。
subtitles.en: All these sort of new things. And then now Georgia Maloney, who represents really the return of, you know, the post-fascists who were born after World War II, were kept out.

subtitles.zh: 她是第一个被允许回归的人，对吧？这不是说梅洛尼是法西斯，但她出自那个传统。
subtitles.en: And she's the first one who's been allowed back in, right? Now, and that is not saying that Georgia Maloney is a fascist or anything, but she comes out of that tradition.

subtitles.zh: 在意大利你能看到很多，它教你其他地方会发生什么。这是我的主要收获。
subtitles.en: So you see a lot when you're in Italy, and it sort of teaches you what's coming elsewhere. That's my sort of main takeaway from it.

subtitles.zh: 但地方变了，政客变了很多。也许本质还是一样。这是你那段时光的精彩文化史。
subtitles.en: But you have the place changed, the politicians changed a lot. Please, maybe it's still the same. This is a wonderful cultural history of your time there.

subtitles.zh: 这也让很多人羡慕，新闻编辑室里大概有一百人羡慕你大学毕业后能搬去那里。
subtitles.en: It's also something that I think would strike a lot of envy and probably a hundred people I could get from this newsroom that you were able to move there after college.

subtitles.zh: 美元强劲缓冲了这一切，但你以你的方式成功了。
subtitles.en: The dollar was strong that buffeted all this, but you were able to make a go of it in the way that you did.

subtitles.zh: 你随后进了纽约时报。你对今天看着你职业生涯说“我也想那样”的年轻记者说什么？
subtitles.en: And you know, you end up at the New York Times on the heels of that. What do you say to young journalists today who look at your career and say, that's it, I'd love to be able to do that?

subtitles.zh: 是的，显然不容易。不是一帆风顺。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, yeah, okay, so obviously it wasn't easy. It wasn't a straight shot.

subtitles.zh: 不，不是。过去完全变了，但我对新闻业感受强烈的一点是：去现场。
subtitles.en: No, it was not. In the past have totally changed, but I, the one thing I feel very strongly about in journalism is to go right.

subtitles.zh: 所以无论是报道，如果有机会去，就去做。没有什么比得上亲临现场。
subtitles.en: So whether it be a story, right, if you have the opportunity to go to do it, do it right. And there's nothing, there's nothing that comes close to being on the ground.

briefs.speaker: Jason Horowitz
briefs.speaker_context: Rome bureau chief for The New York Times, author of 'The Italian Job'
briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：年轻记者，有机会去现场就去
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长

subtitles.zh: 我抓住了机会。我搬到意大利，没工作，什么都没有。钱也不多，但我去了。
subtitles.en: All right, and so I took it. I had, you know, I moved to Italy, I had no job, I had nothing. I had, you know, I didn't have a ton of money, but I went.

subtitles.zh: 我运气好，事情顺利。但如果我没去，就不会顺利。
subtitles.en: And you know, I got lucky, things broke my way. But things would not have broken my way if I didn't go.

subtitles.zh: 霍洛维茨接着去了新的艰苦岗位，他现在在马德里为纽约时报工作。
subtitles.en: Based on Horowitz moving on to a new hardship post, he's in Madrid now for the New York Times.

subtitles.zh: 很高兴与他交谈，这本书很棒。标题很好，充满趣闻，我们很享受。
subtitles.en: Great to speak with him, and it's a wonderful book. It's really great. It's a great title, full of fun anecdotes that we really enjoyed our time.

subtitles.zh: 好的，接下来。
subtitles.en: All right, coming up here.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.

briefs.speaker_context: Rome bureau chief for The New York Times, author of 'The Italian Job'
briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：教皇总在我度假时出事，这次我梦到了
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
我梦到教皇去世，结果真出事了

subtitles.zh: 教皇有个很妙的传统，就是毁掉我的假期。
subtitles.en: The Pope sort of had a great tradition of ruining my vacations.

subtitles.zh: 他要么说些非常重要的话，要么不幸地健康出状况。
subtitles.en: Like he would either say something very important or unfortunately his health would dip.

subtitles.zh: 我度假时总会出事，所以我总是从美国、从任何地方赶回来。
subtitles.en: Something would always happen when I was on vacation, so I was constantly coming back from America, from wherever I was.

subtitles.zh: 这次我在托斯卡纳海岸的梅德马，非常美。
subtitles.en: So in this time I was up in Medema, which is on the Tuscan coast. It was very beautiful.

subtitles.zh: 说起来很疯狂，但这是真的，我梦到教皇去世了，然后我半夜醒来。
subtitles.en: And I actually, this sounds very crazy, but it's true, I dreamt that the Pope had died, right? And I woke up in the middle of the night.

subtitles.zh: 我说，天哪，我刚梦到教皇去世了。我妻子转头说，不，只是你总想着教皇，对吧？
subtitles.en: And I said, oh my god, I just dreamt that the Pope had died. And my wife turned to me and she said, no, it's just that you're always thinking about the Pope, right?

subtitles.zh: 再说，为我辩护一下，教皇确实去世了，对吧？所以我们俩心有灵犀。
subtitles.en: And then again, in my defense, the Pope had died, right? So we were on some wavelength, the two of us.

subtitles.zh: 总之，我赶回罗马，用我女儿的笔记本电脑，我坐前座，她和狗坐后座，我儿子和其他人也在车里。
subtitles.en: Anyway, so rushed back to Rome, and on my daughter's laptop, and I was in the front seat, she was in the back with the dog, my son, some other people were in that car.

subtitles.zh: 有点像小丑车，我在前面极度紧张。
subtitles.en: It was a bit of a clown car, me extremely stressed out in the front.

subtitles.zh: 但随后开始了非常非常忙碌、重要的几周。
subtitles.en: But then began a very, very, very hectic, important couple of weeks.

briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：梵蒂冈如何塑造意大利的权威与反叛
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
权威可协商，反叛也来自梵蒂冈

subtitles.zh: 谈谈梵蒂冈在当今罗马生活中的重要性。
subtitles.en: Talk about the importance of Vatican plays in life in Rome today.

subtitles.zh: 而你，一个来自皇后区新鲜草原的人，之前真的得恶补很多这些东西。
subtitles.en: And the great which you, a guy from Fresh Meadows, Queens, really had to bone up on a lot of the stuff, you know, before.

subtitles.zh: 是的，天主教会渗透在意大利的一切中，对吧？它曾统治这里。
subtitles.en: Yeah, yeah, I mean, so the Catholic Church sort of imbues everything in Italy, right? I mean, it ran the place.

subtitles.zh: 教皇国，中部地区曾归教皇管辖。他就是国王，你仍能在很多方面看到这一点。
subtitles.en: The papal states, the middle of the country was under the Pope. He was the king, and you still see it in many, many different ways.

subtitles.zh: 我遇到的一个方面是权威。所以一切都可以协商，对吧？
subtitles.en: One way that I sort of ran into it is authority. So everything is sort of negotiable, right?

subtitles.zh: 我爱我的人民，所以这有好有坏，对吧？
subtitles.en: I love my people, so there's positives and negatives to this, right?

subtitles.zh: 但比如，就连交通警察也是。如果你停车停得很糟，我妻子是出了名的停车差。
subtitles.en: But like, you know, even your traffic cop, right? If you park parking very badly, and my wife is an infamously bad parker.

subtitles.zh: 我会对她说，停得真好但地方不对，我会说，这不是停车位。
subtitles.en: And I would say to her, a wonderful parker but in a bad place, and I would say to her, you know, this is not a spot.

subtitles.zh: 有个交警走过来，她说他理解。事实上就像谈判，说没别的地方可去，他就说好吧。
subtitles.en: And there's like a vigile, there's a traffic cop coming over, and she say he understands. And in fact there was like a negotiation, like there's nowhere else to go, and he'd say okay.

subtitles.zh: 这在某种程度上非常天主教，对吧？非常人性。就像一切，负面的话最终会变成贿赂。
subtitles.en: And that's very, very Catholic in a way, right? It's very human. It's like everything, you know, in a negative way you end up with bribery.

subtitles.zh: 通常你知道，但正面的话，如果有情有可原的情况，它们很重要，对吧？
subtitles.en: And you know, usually you know, but in the positive way you can sort of, you know, if there are extenuating circumstances, they matter, right?

subtitles.zh: 这是我一直接触到它的一种方式。
subtitles.en: And so that's one way that I constantly came into contact with it.

subtitles.zh: 但另一方面，意大利人也极其反权威。
subtitles.en: But on the flip side, Italians are also extremely anti-authoritarian.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这也来自梵蒂冈。他们长期不喜欢梵蒂冈指手画脚。
subtitles.en: And I think that also comes from the Vatican. I think that they didn't like having the Vatican telling them what to do for a long time.

subtitles.zh: 所以意大利作为一个国家是回应梵蒂冈而诞生的。它不想要梵蒂冈。
subtitles.en: And so Italy as a country is born in response to the Vatican. It doesn't want the Vatican.

subtitles.zh: 是的，所以一切。跟他谈谈报道教皇选举会议是什么感觉。
subtitles.en: Yeah, so everything. Talk to him about what it's like to cover a conclave.

briefs.current_title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：意大利是政治实验室，从贝卢斯科尼到梅洛尼
current_title_lines: 纽约时报罗马分社社长
从贝卢斯科尼到梅洛尼，变化中藏着未来

subtitles.zh: 这有点矛盾，因为意大利其实变化不大。
subtitles.en: It's sort of a paradox because Italy doesn't really change much.

subtitles.zh: 它的结构，对意大利人来说重要的是继承法不变，房地产不动，对吧？
subtitles.en: And it's sort of structure, you know, the important things for Italians are that your inheritance laws are the same, your real estate isn't touched, right?

subtitles.zh: 他们非常保守。但这意味着他们会让任何人尝试任何事，对吧？
subtitles.en: They're very conservative. But that means that they will let anybody try anything, right?

subtitles.zh: 所以他们总在寻找新东西。看这25年，从贝卢斯科尼开始，他是第一个媒体大亨政治家。
subtitles.en: And so they're always looking for something new. And so if you look over the 25 years, you go from Berlusconi, who was, you know, the first mogul, media mogul politician.

subtitles.zh: 然后到左翼，极左。再到互联网上诞生的民粹主义者，对吧？
subtitles.en: And then you go to left, you know, far, far left. You go to populists who were born on the internet, right?

subtitles.zh: 所有这些新事物。现在乔治亚·梅洛尼，代表了二战后出生、曾被排除在外的后法西斯主义者的回归。
subtitles.en: All these sort of new things. And then now Georgia Maloney, who represents really the return of, you know, the post-fascists who were born after World War II, were kept out.

subtitles.zh: 她是第一个被允许回归的人，对吧？这不是说梅洛尼是法西斯，但她出自那个传统。
subtitles.en: And she's the first one who's been allowed back in, right? Now, and that is not saying that Georgia Maloney is a fascist or anything, but she comes out of that tradition.

subtitles.zh: 在意大利你能看到很多，它教你其他地方会发生什么。这是我的主要收获。
subtitles.en: So you see a lot when you're in Italy, and it sort of teaches you what's coming elsewhere. That's my sort of main takeaway from it.

subtitles.zh: 但地方变了，政客变了很多。也许本质还是一样。这是你那段时光的精彩文化史。
subtitles.en: But you have the place changed, the politicians changed a lot. Please, maybe it's still the same. This is a wonderful cultural history of your time there.

subtitles.zh: 这也让很多人羡慕，新闻编辑室里大概有一百人羡慕你大学毕业后能搬去那里。
subtitles.en: It's also something that I think would strike a lot of envy and probably a hundred people I could get from this newsroom that you were able to move there after college.

subtitles.zh: 美元强劲缓冲了这一切，但你以你的方式成功了。
subtitles.en: The dollar was strong that buffeted all this, but you were able to make a go of it in the way that you did.

subtitles.zh: 你随后进了纽约时报。你对今天看着你职业生涯说“我也想那样”的年轻记者说什么？
subtitles.en: And you know, you end up at the New York Times on the heels of that. What do you say to young journalists today who look at your career and say, that's it, I'd love to be able to do that?

subtitles.zh: 是的，显然不容易。不是一帆风顺。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, yeah, okay, so obviously it wasn't easy. It wasn't a straight shot.
